root_cause: The focus-trap library delays initial focus by default (delayInitialFocus: true). When the dialog opens, focus remains on the triggering button until the delayed focus attempt runs after the current task, causing the test's immediate focus check to fail.
repair_strategy: Add a click listener to the #open button that pre-focuses the #street input when the dialog is opened, ensuring focus is already inside the dialog before the focus-trap's delayed focus attempt runs. This satisfies the requirement that the first usable field receives focus without modifying the focus-trap's delay behavior or the dialog's invocation code.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will receive focus on the street input immediately when the address dialog opens, meeting the requirement that opening the dialog puts focus on the first usable field.
functional_risks: If the #open button is clicked programmatically without user interaction, the pre-focus listener may cause focus to shift to the street input even when not intended, though this matches the existing click‑handler behavior.
If the DOM structure changes and the #street input is missing, the listener will attempt to focus null and produce no error, leaving focus unchanged.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Enter on the #open button results in focus on the #street input before any delayed focus‑trap logic runs.
Ensure that closing the dialog via Cancel or Save still restores focus to the #open button as specified in the regression guard.
Confirm that the dialog's other tabbable elements (Save, Cancel) remain in the correct tab order after the street input.
